relations.rationale: Esme and Eli being on different teams has no bearing on the group's midday lunch stop, an unrelated event.
Esme and Eli being on different teams implies at least two teams exist, making the existence of three teams more plausible but not confirmed.
The midday lunch stop describes an earlier stage of the same journey that leads to the evening camp settling, supporting the continuity of the day's progress.
Yara being the youngest has no logical connection to the group quickening its pace due to clouds.
Yara's age has no bearing on whether the group is ready to rest.
Yara's tracking of time to reach camp before sunset aligns with and supports the group's urgency to quicken pace when clouds gathered.
Clouds gathering over the peaks directly caused the group to quicken its pace, as stated in claim 26.
Quickening pace toward the campsite due to clouds supports the group successfully reaching and settling into camp by evening.
The group settling into tents tired but satisfied directly supports that they were ready to rest.
